images.title: 12 slips through 4 and 6 but not 24
images.purpose: Shows the combined divisibility trap in its simplest state: 12 passes the gates for 4 and 6 but fails the gate for 24.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no characters, no extra text. Three gates in one row with a number token moving through them, and a result under each gate.
images.exact_structure: A reddish purple (#CC79A7) round token holding 12 at the left. Three equal archway gates in a row, left to right labelled ÷ 4, ÷ 6 and ÷ 24 on their tops. Under the first two gates the word pass in green (#009E73). Under the third gate the word fail in vermilion (#D55E00), and the token is shown stopped in front of the third gate inside a small box labelled trapped. A thin dark dashed path runs from the token through the first two gates to the third. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: 12 is divisible by 4 and by 6 but not by 24, because 4 and 6 share a factor 2.

images.context: 12 = 4 × 3 = 6 × 2; 12 is not a multiple of 24; LCM of 4 and 6 is 12.

image_decisions.why: The doer's tool is a row of test gates; the trapped 12 is its core move in the simplest case.
